text:
Predicates:
Hydrocarbon(x) ::: x is a hydrocarbon.
Organic(x) ::: x is an organic compound.
Alkane(x) ::: x is an alkane.
ChemicalCompound(x) ::: x is a chemical compound.
ContainsCarbon(x) ::: x contains carbon.
ContainsOnlyOneElement(x) ::: x contains only one element.
Mixture ::: the mixture.

Premises:
∀x (Hydrocarbon(x) → Organic(x)) ::: All hydrocarbons are organic compounds.
∀x (Alkane(x) → Hydrocarbon(x)) ::: All alkanes are hydrocarbons.
∀x (Organic(x) → ChemicalCompound(x)) ::: All organic compounds are chemical compounds.
∀x (Organic(x) → ContainsCarbon(x)) ::: All organic compounds contain carbon.
∀x (ChemicalCompound(x) → ¬ContainsOnlyOneElement(x)) ::: No chemical compounds contain only one element.
(ChemicalCompound(Mixture) ∧ ContainsOnlyOneElement(Mixture)) ⊕ ¬(ChemicalCompound(Mixture) ∨ ContainsOnlyOneElement(Mixture)) ::: The mixture either both is a chemical compound and contains only one element, or neither.

Conclusion:
Alkane(Mixture) ∧ ContainsCarbon(Mixture) ::: The mixture is an alkane and contains carbon.
